title: Today
purpose: When I sit down in the morning, or a number jumps during the day, open Today to know where the business is losing the most money, what to do first and what is waiting on me, without reading 10 dashboards.
fires: The morning tour of 5 to 10 dashboards, the agency's Monday call as the first word on the numbers, decisions buried in Slack, email and WhatsApp, and the habit of checking the phone 20 times a day.
not_for: A store under about $20k a month in sales, or a founder who already works every channel by hand every day; a weekly look is enough there.

jobs.job: When I sit down in the morning with 20 minutes before the team starts asking me things, tell me the one place the business is losing the most money right now, in dollars, so I spend today on that and not on whatever is loudest
jobs.circumstance: Weekday morning, laptop open, Slack already busy, 5 dashboards unread, a team or agency waiting for direction

progress.functional: know which step from ad click to repeat order is costing the most this week, and how much
progress.emotional: stop the low hum of worry that something is broken and I have not seen it
progress.social: walk into the standup with a clear call instead of asking everyone what they think

jobs.hire_today: gut feel plus a morning tour of Shopify, Meta, Google and email dashboards; or the agency's weekly report
jobs.fire: the dashboard tour and the wait for the agency's report

forces.push: every day a leak goes unseen costs real money, and the loudest problem is rarely the biggest
forces.pull: one named leak with a dollar figure and the date it started
forces.habit: I have always opened Shopify first and trusted my read of it
forces.anxiety: what if it names the wrong leak and I send the team after a ghost

jobs.little_hire: every weekday morning, before the first meeting

watch.metric: dollars at stake at the weakest step from visit to repeat order, 7 day, against its own 4 week median
watch.source: Shopify, GA4 and ad platforms, joined in the brand brain

drives.metric: gross profit per week

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: checkout completion is 8 points under its 4 week median, about $6,200 a week at stake, found on day 9. After: the leak is named on day 1 and the stake is under $1,000 within 7 days.
jobs.not_for: an owner whose store runs on one channel they already watch every hour

jobs.job: When yesterday's orders are in, tell me whether yesterday made money after product cost, shipping, fees, returns and ads, so I know if I can keep spending today
jobs.circumstance: Early morning, yesterday's revenue looks good in Shopify, ad spend was high, and no one will know the profit until the bookkeeper closes the month

progress.functional: know yesterday's gross profit after ads, in dollars, and the 7 day trend
progress.emotional: stop feeling rich on revenue and poor at month end
progress.social: answer a partner's "are we making money" with a number, not a feeling

jobs.hire_today: Nothing daily. A bookkeeper's profit and loss 3 to 6 weeks after month end, or a spreadsheet some weeks. Owners do nothing daily because the costs sit in 4 places and joining them takes an hour
jobs.fire: waiting for the month-end close; the spreadsheet rebuilt on Sundays

forces.push: a month of spending at a loss is found only after the cash is gone
forces.pull: one profit number each morning that already counts the costs I forget
forces.habit: revenue in Shopify is the number I have always looked at
forces.anxiety: what if the costs in it are wrong and I trust a profit that is not real

jobs.little_hire: every morning, and after any big spend day

watch.metric: gross profit after ad spend, yesterday and 7 day
watch.source: Shopify orders, product costs in the brand brain, ad platforms

drives.metric: contribution margin per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: profit is known 5 weeks after month end. After: profit after ads is known each morning, and 2 loss-making days in a row trigger a spend review the same day.
jobs.not_for: a store whose product costs are not entered yet; fix the costs first or the number will lie

jobs.job: When a stock payment, a card bill and payroll land in the same fortnight, tell me if cash covers the next 4 weeks of bills, stock and ads, so I am not surprised by a bounced payment
jobs.circumstance: Mid-month, a supplier deposit due, ad cards charging daily, the bank balance looks fine today but big payments are queued

progress.functional: know the lowest cash balance in the next 4 weeks and the day it hits
progress.emotional: sleep without doing bank math in my head at night
progress.social: tell a supplier or lender a date I can keep

jobs.hire_today: the bank app balance, a cash sheet the bookkeeper updates monthly, or gut feel
jobs.fire: the bank balance used as a forecast; the monthly cash sheet

forces.push: one short fortnight can stop ads or stall a stock order
forces.pull: a dated low point with the payments that cause it
forces.habit: I look at the balance and do the math myself
forces.anxiety: what if a payment is missing from the forecast and the low point is worse than shown

jobs.little_hire: every Monday, and before any stock order or big ad push

watch.metric: lowest projected cash balance over the next 28 days
watch.source: bank feed, bills due and ad spend in the brand brain

drives.metric: cash on hand at month end

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a $38k gap is found 3 days before a supplier payment. After: the low point is known 3 weeks ahead and the payment is moved or ads trimmed in time.
jobs.not_for: a store with 6 months of cash in the bank and no stock orders; a monthly look is enough

jobs.job: When something breaks during the day, like checkout failing, a campaign spending double or the site going down, tell me within the hour, so I stop the loss before tomorrow's report
jobs.circumstance: Mid-afternoon, I am in a supplier call or on the road, a spend cap failed or a payment app broke, and orders stopped 2 hours ago

progress.functional: know that a number crossed its line, which one, and the dollars per hour at stake
progress.emotional: stop the fear that the store is broken while I am away
progress.social: be the one who caught it, not the one a customer told

jobs.hire_today: Nothing reliable. A customer email, a team member who happens to notice, or an app alert that fires for everything and gets muted
jobs.fire: learning of a break from customers or from the next morning's report

forces.push: a broken checkout on a sale day costs thousands per hour
forces.pull: one alert, only when a real line is crossed, with the person who fixes it named
forces.habit: I check the Shopify app on my phone every hour
forces.anxiety: what if it fires all day for nothing and I start to ignore it

jobs.little_hire: any day a number crosses a line; ideally rare

watch.metric: hours from a break to the first action
watch.source: Shopify orders per hour, ad spend per hour, site uptime check

drives.metric: revenue lost to breaks per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a failed payment app went 7 hours unseen, about $4,100 lost. After: breaks are acted on within 1 hour and monthly losses fall under $500.
jobs.not_for: a store with under 20 orders a day, where a break is hard to tell from a quiet hour

jobs.job: When people are waiting on me across Slack, email, WhatsApp and the agency's threads, show me every decision that needs me in one place, oldest and costliest first, so no one is blocked by me
jobs.circumstance: Any morning, 4 chat apps, an agency, 2 freelancers and a team all waiting on approvals, and I cannot remember who asked what

progress.functional: clear the decisions that block work, starting with the ones that cost most to delay
progress.emotional: stop the guilt of being the bottleneck
progress.social: be the owner who answers fast, not the one people chase

jobs.hire_today: memory, starred emails, an assistant, or the agency chasing me
jobs.fire: the scattered threads and the weekly "any updates?" chase

forces.push: work stalls for days on a one-line yes
forces.pull: one queue with the cost of waiting on each item
forces.habit: I answer whoever pings me loudest
forces.anxiety: what if something important sits outside the queue and I miss it

watch.metric: median days a decision waits on the owner

drives.metric: ideas shipped per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: decisions wait 6 days on average, 3 are older than 2 weeks. After: the median wait is under 1 day.
jobs.not_for: a founder who does every task alone, with no one waiting on them

jobs.job: When I have a dozen possible fixes and one morning, rank what to do first by the money each is worth, and let me approve, hand off or park each in a minute, so nothing sits half-decided for weeks
jobs.circumstance: Monday morning, a backlog of ideas from the agency, the team and my own notes, no order to them, and a few free hours

progress.functional: decide the order of work by dollars at stake and effort
progress.emotional: stop the guilt of a to-do list that only grows
progress.social: show the team and agency why their idea was parked, with a reason, so no one feels ignored

jobs.hire_today: a notebook or Notion list, the agency's recommendations, or whatever the last person asked for
jobs.fire: the unranked backlog, and the agency setting the order of work

forces.push: good ideas die in the list while the easy ones get done
forces.pull: a short ranked list with the dollars and the effort on each line
forces.habit: I pick by feel and by who shouted last
forces.anxiety: what if the ranking favors what is easy to measure over what matters

jobs.little_hire: every Monday, and when a new idea lands

watch.metric: ideas decided within 7 days of being raised, and dollars at stake on the undecided ones

drives.metric: gross profit per week

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 40 open ideas, 12 older than 30 days. After: every idea decided or parked with a reason within 7 days.
jobs.not_for: a solo founder with 3 ideas in their head and no team to hand them to

jobs.job: When I run an agency and open my laptop, tell me which client needs me first today and why, so I call them before they call me
jobs.circumstance: Agency owner, 12 client brands, morning, one client's sales dropped overnight and I do not know it yet

progress.functional: rank clients by dollars at risk and days since the problem started
progress.emotional: stop dreading an angry client call I did not see coming
progress.social: look on top of the account in front of the client

jobs.hire_today: account managers' Friday updates, a shared sheet, or waiting for the client's email
jobs.fire: the Friday round-up and the tour of each client's dashboards

forces.push: one surprised client can cost the account
forces.pull: one list across every client, worst first, with the reason
forces.habit: each account manager watches their own clients
forces.anxiety: what if a client's data is missing and it looks fine when it is not

jobs.little_hire: every morning, for the agency owner and each account lead

watch.metric: client problems raised by us before the client raised them, 30 day

drives.metric: client retention, 12 month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 of 5 client problems last month were raised by the client first. After: 5 of 5 raised by us first.
jobs.not_for: a single-brand owner; this job only exists across several brands

jobs.job: When a best seller is selling faster than planned, warn me while there is still time to reorder, so I do not pay for ads that send buyers to a sold-out page
jobs.circumstance: A good week, one product selling 30 percent above plan, supplier lead time 8 weeks, and no one checking stock days against lead time

progress.functional: know days of stock left against reorder lead time for each top product
progress.emotional: stop the sick feeling of seeing "sold out" on the best seller
progress.social: avoid telling the agency to pause ads because we ran out

jobs.hire_today: an ops lead's spreadsheet, the supplier's reminder, or noticing when it hits zero
jobs.fire: the stock sheet checked monthly; finding out at zero

forces.push: a stockout on a best seller loses sales and resets what the ad platform has learned
forces.pull: a dated warning with the reorder quantity and the cash it needs
forces.habit: we reorder when it looks low
forces.anxiety: what if the forecast is too high and I tie up cash in stock

jobs.little_hire: weekly, and any day a product sells above plan

watch.metric: days of stock left against supplier lead days, top 10 products
watch.source: Shopify inventory, lead times in the brand brain

drives.metric: stockout days on top products per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the top product sold out for 19 days last quarter. After: no top product runs out, and reorders go in with 2 weeks of slack.
jobs.not_for: a made-to-order or print-on-demand store with no stock to run out of

jobs.job: When a number looks odd, tell me which numbers I cannot trust today and why, so I do not make a call on a broken pixel or a missing feed
jobs.circumstance: Morning, Meta says 40 purchases, Shopify says 22, GA4 shows half the traffic, and the team is about to act on one of them

progress.functional: know which sources are stale, broken or disagree, and by how much
progress.emotional: stop the doubt that every number might be wrong
progress.social: avoid a confident call in front of the team that rests on a broken number

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. Owners assume the numbers are fine until an agency or a big miss shows otherwise, because checking every source by hand takes hours
jobs.fire: blind trust in whichever dashboard opened first

forces.push: decisions made on broken data waste budget for weeks
forces.pull: a short list of what is unreadable today and what it blocks
forces.habit: the dashboards have always looked fine
forces.anxiety: what if the check itself is wrong and flags good data

jobs.little_hire: every morning, before reading anything else

watch.metric: sources passing the daily trust check, and the gap between ad platform and store purchases, yesterday

drives.metric: share of ad spend decided on trusted numbers

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a pixel broke for 9 days before anyone saw it. After: breaks are flagged the next morning and no budget move is made on a failed source.
jobs.not_for: a store that runs no paid ads and reads only Shopify

jobs.job: When I have a plain question like "what did we make on the 3-pack last week", answer it from my own numbers in a minute, so I do not wait days for an analyst or give up asking
jobs.circumstance: Mid-afternoon, a thought during a call, the agency takes 2 days to answer, so I stop asking

progress.functional: get a correct answer with the source shown
progress.emotional: stop feeling locked out of my own data
progress.social: answer the team on the spot

jobs.hire_today: a request to an analyst or the agency, a Shopify export, or not asking at all
jobs.fire: export-and-pivot sessions and waiting on the agency

forces.push: questions go unasked, so decisions are made on guesses
forces.pull: an answer with the number and where it came from
forces.habit: I ask the agency and wait
forces.anxiety: what if the answer sounds right and is wrong

watch.metric: questions answered within 5 minutes with a source, 30 day

drives.metric: decisions made on numbers, not guesses

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a 2 day wait per question, and most are never asked. After: 20 questions a week answered in minutes.
jobs.not_for: a question about data that is not connected yet; it should say unavailable, not guess

jobs.job: When the agency says the account is doing well, let me check their claim against my own store numbers, so I stop paying for work I cannot verify
jobs.circumstance: Monthly agency call, their deck shows platform return up, and my bank account does not feel it

progress.functional: compare the agency's reported results with store revenue and profit for the same period
progress.emotional: stop the unease of trusting a report I cannot check
progress.social: hold the agency to account without a fight

jobs.hire_today: trust, or a second agency's audit
jobs.fire: the agency's deck as the only view

forces.push: agency fees and ad budget are my biggest costs
forces.pull: the same period in my numbers next to theirs
forces.habit: I nod along on the call
forces.anxiety: what if this starts a fight with an agency I need

watch.metric: gap between agency-reported revenue and store-recorded revenue from paid traffic, 30 day

drives.metric: share of ad spend on channels that pay back in the store

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the agency reports $4 back per $1, the store shows $2.10. After: the gap is on the table and budget follows the store.
jobs.not_for: a brand that runs its own ads in house

jobs.job: When I am away from my desk and a decision is blocking the team, let me decide from my phone in one reply, so work does not wait for me to get back
jobs.circumstance: Travelling, at a trade show or with family, a buyer needs a yes on a budget move or a draft

progress.functional: approve, reject or park with a reason in under a minute
progress.emotional: stop feeling chained to the laptop
progress.social: keep the team moving without them feeling they bothered me

jobs.hire_today: WhatsApp messages with screenshots, phone calls, or an ops lead who guesses
jobs.fire: screenshots in chat and "can you jump on a call"

forces.push: a day away stalls every open decision
forces.pull: a short card with the number and the ask, answered by reply
forces.habit: I say "I will look tonight"
forces.anxiety: what if I approve something on a small screen that I would have caught on a big one

jobs.little_hire: any day away from the desk

watch.metric: decisions made within 4 hours while away

drives.metric: median days a decision waits on the owner

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 days away means 3 days of stalled approvals. After: 80 percent of decisions are made within 4 hours from the phone.
jobs.not_for: a decision that moves more than a set amount of money; that one should wait for the full numbers

jobs.job: When a number jumps or drops, tell me whether we caused it or something outside did, like a holiday, a platform outage, a rival's sale or the weather, so I do not take credit or blame for luck
jobs.circumstance: Tuesday, sales up 25 percent after a new ad went live, and it is also a long weekend

progress.functional: separate our own changes from outside events for any big move
progress.emotional: stop swinging between pride and panic on every move
progress.social: give the team or client an honest reason, not a story

jobs.hire_today: gut feel, the agency's explanation, or a same-week-last-year check in a spreadsheet
jobs.fire: the agency's version of why

forces.push: wrong credit sends more money to things that did not work
forces.pull: each big move shown next to what else happened that week
forces.habit: the last thing we changed gets the credit
forces.anxiety: what if it calls a real win luck and I stop doing it

jobs.little_hire: any day a number moves more than its normal range

watch.metric: big moves with a named cause, checked against the same week last year, 28 day
watch.source: store orders, ad platforms, calendar in the brand brain

drives.metric: share of budget moved on a confirmed cause

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a holiday bump was credited to a new ad and its budget tripled. After: the holiday is named on day 1 and budget moves wait for a clean read.
jobs.not_for: a store too new to have a year of history to compare against

jobs.job: When the weekly team or agency meeting starts, give everyone the same numbers, so we spend the hour deciding and not arguing about whose number is right
jobs.circumstance: Weekly meeting, the agency shows Meta's number, the team shows Shopify's, and 20 minutes go to reconciling

progress.functional: one agreed number per question, with its source
progress.emotional: stop the tension of every meeting starting with a fight
progress.social: the agency and team trust the same facts

jobs.hire_today: the agency's slide deck, or each person's own export
jobs.fire: the agency deck as the source of truth

forces.push: meetings end with no decisions
forces.pull: one page everyone reads from
forces.habit: each side brings its own numbers
forces.anxiety: what if the agency feels its work is being judged by a new number

watch.metric: decisions made per meeting, and minutes spent reconciling numbers

drives.metric: decisions per week

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 20 of 60 minutes are spent on whose number is right. After: under 5 minutes, with 3 decisions made each week.
jobs.not_for: a founder with no team or agency meeting

jobs.job: When I have just connected my store and doubt any tool can tell me something new, show me 3 things about my own business I did not know, with dollars, so I can decide whether this is worth my time
jobs.circumstance: Day 1, store and ads just connected, burned before by dashboards that told me what I already knew

progress.functional: see 3 real findings about my store, each with a stake
progress.emotional: move from doubt to curiosity
progress.social: show my partner or team a finding worth talking about

jobs.hire_today: a free audit from an agency, a consultant, or my own gut
jobs.fire: the free agency audit that exists to sell a retainer

forces.push: I have paid for tools that told me nothing
forces.pull: a finding I can check myself in 10 minutes
forces.habit: I already know my store
forces.anxiety: what if the findings are generic advice any blog would give

jobs.little_hire: once at connect, then each quarter

watch.metric: findings the owner marks new and true in the first week

drives.metric: dollars at stake acted on in the first 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: no outside view of the store. After: 3 findings worth $9k a month named in week 1, and 1 acted on.
jobs.not_for: a store with under 3 months of orders; there is not enough history to find anything real

jobs.job: When one review, complaint or order problem could blow up, like a safety claim, a viral post or an angry wholesale buyer, put it in front of me today, so a small thing does not become public
jobs.circumstance: A 1-star review mentions a rash, a TikTok comment is gaining likes, and support is unsure whether to escalate

progress.functional: see the few single items that carry risk above their size
progress.emotional: stop fearing the one thing no one told me about
progress.social: respond as the owner before it becomes a story

jobs.hire_today: the support lead's judgement, or finding it when it is already public
jobs.fire: the rule of "support handles it"

forces.push: one ignored item can cost more than a bad month
forces.pull: a short list of single items with why each is risky
forces.habit: support escalates only when they think to
forces.anxiety: what if it floods me with small complaints

watch.metric: risky single items seen by the owner within 24 hours

drives.metric: complaints that reached press or 1,000 views, per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a product safety review sat 11 days before the owner saw it. After: it is seen the same day and answered within 24 hours.
jobs.not_for: a brand with a full-time support lead who already escalates well

jobs.job: When I have a call with an investor, supplier, platform rep or agency in an hour, give me a 1-page brief with the numbers that matter to that person, so I walk in prepared
jobs.circumstance: A calendar reminder, 60 minutes to the call, and the numbers are in 5 places

progress.functional: have the 5 numbers and 3 open points for that meeting
progress.emotional: stop the scramble before calls
progress.social: look like I know my business cold

jobs.hire_today: 30 minutes of pulling numbers, an assistant, or winging it
jobs.fire: the pre-call scramble

forces.push: bad prep costs terms with suppliers and trust with investors
forces.pull: a brief ready before the call
forces.habit: I pull what I can remember
forces.anxiety: what if a number in the brief is stale

watch.metric: calls with a brief ready 30 minutes ahead, 30 day

drives.metric: supplier terms and investor follow-ups won

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 20 minutes of prep per call, often skipped. After: a brief for every call and prep under 5 minutes.
jobs.not_for: an owner with few outside calls, where memory is enough

jobs.job: When I have checked the dashboards 15 times before lunch, tell me plainly that nothing needs me today, so I can stop checking and work on the business
jobs.circumstance: A normal day, an anxious founder, phone in hand, refreshing Shopify and Ads Manager between tasks

progress.functional: know that every number is inside its normal range
progress.emotional: get relief from the urge to check
progress.social: be present with the team and family instead of on the phone

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. The checking is the workaround, and it costs hours a week
jobs.fire: the hourly refresh habit

forces.push: hours lost and focus broken every day
forces.pull: a clear all-clear I can trust
forces.habit: checking feels like being in control
forces.anxiety: what if the all-clear is wrong on the day something breaks

jobs.little_hire: every day, most of all the quiet ones

watch.metric: owner visits to store and ad dashboards per day
watch.source: owner's own log in the brand brain

drives.metric: owner hours on planned work per week

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 15 dashboard checks a day, about 1 hour. After: 2 checks a day, with alerts trusted for the rest.
jobs.not_for: an owner who does not check compulsively; they will not miss this

jobs.job: When orders ship late or replies to customers pile up, tell me before reviews say so, so a slow week does not turn into 1-star reviews
jobs.circumstance: The warehouse is short on staff, 300 tickets are open, and the owner hears only when reviews drop

progress.functional: know shipping days and first reply hours against what we promise
progress.emotional: stop being blindsided by angry reviews
progress.social: protect the brand's name with customers

jobs.hire_today: the 3PL's weekly report, or the support lead's word
jobs.fire: waiting for reviews to tell me

forces.push: late orders drive refunds, disputes and bad reviews
forces.pull: a warning when promise times slip
forces.habit: support and the 3PL handle it
forces.anxiety: what if the 3PL's data feed is late too

watch.metric: orders shipped on time and first reply hours, 7 day

drives.metric: review rating, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: on-time shipping fell to 78 percent for 2 weeks before anyone saw it. After: it is flagged on day 2 and fixed within the week.
jobs.not_for: a store where the owner packs and answers every order by hand

jobs.job: When a number slips a little each week, flag it after 2 weeks running, so I catch a slow leak while it is still cheap to fix
jobs.circumstance: No single bad day, but add to cart has dropped a little for 3 weeks, and every daily check looked normal

progress.functional: see a trend that daily noise hides
progress.emotional: stop the dread of finding a 6-month slide in the quarterly review
progress.social: raise it early with the team instead of explaining a big drop later

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. A slow slide never trips a daily check, and no one compares weeks by hand
jobs.fire: the daily look that hides trends

forces.push: small slides add up to bad quarters
forces.pull: a note after 2 weeks in the same direction, with the size so far
forces.habit: if today looks normal, it is fine
forces.anxiety: what if it flags normal wobble and wastes the team's time

watch.metric: steps moving the same way 2 weeks running, and the dollar impact so far

drives.metric: gross profit per week

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: conversion slid from 2.4 to 1.9 percent over 10 weeks before anyone noticed. After: the slide is flagged at week 2, at 2.2 percent.
jobs.not_for: a store with so few orders that weekly numbers swing by chance

jobs.job: When I look back at last quarter, show me what my own decisions actually earned or cost, so I learn which instincts to trust
jobs.circumstance: Quarter end, I made 30 calls on price, ads and stock, and I remember the wins

progress.functional: see each past decision with its result in dollars
progress.emotional: build confidence on proof, not memory
progress.social: show a partner or the team a record, not a story

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. Decisions live in chat threads and no one follows them up, because it takes time and nobody likes finding their own misses
jobs.fire: memory as the record

forces.push: repeating bad calls costs money every quarter
forces.pull: a list of decisions with what each one earned
forces.habit: I remember the good calls
forces.anxiety: what if my calls look bad next to the record

watch.metric: decisions with a measured result, and dollars earned by them, 90 day

drives.metric: gross profit per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: no record of 30 calls. After: 25 of 30 have a result, and 2 kinds of call that lost money are stopped.
jobs.not_for: an owner who does not want the record kept; it only works if every call is logged

jobs.job: When a platform changes something, like an ad account restriction, a payout hold, a policy update or an app outage, tell me today what it means for us, so I do not find out from a dead sales day
jobs.circumstance: Meta disables an ad account, or Shopify changes checkout, and the email sits in an inbox no one reads

progress.functional: know which platform notices affect us and what to do next
progress.emotional: stop the fear of a surprise shutdown
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: Nothing reliable. Notices land in shared inboxes and get read late, because most of them are noise
jobs.fire: the shared inbox as the alarm

forces.push: a restricted account or a payout hold stops revenue at once
forces.pull: only the notices that affect us, with the next step
forces.habit: someone will see the email
forces.anxiety: what if it misses a notice that came by a channel it does not read

watch.metric: hours from a platform notice to the first action

drives.metric: days of lost ad delivery or payouts per year

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: an ad account was restricted 2 days before anyone saw it. After: it is acted on within 2 hours.
jobs.not_for: a store on one platform with no paid ads

jobs.job: When revenue is up, tell me if new customers are growing or if the same people are just buying more, so I do not mistake a loyal base for growth
jobs.circumstance: End of week, revenue up 12 percent, ad spend up 20 percent, repeat buyers flooding in on an email offer

progress.functional: split revenue into new and returning buyers, and see the cost per new buyer
progress.emotional: stop the false comfort of a good revenue week
progress.social: tell an investor or partner the real growth story

jobs.hire_today: the agency's revenue report, or a Shopify report I rarely open
jobs.fire: revenue as the only growth number

forces.push: a store that stops finding new buyers shrinks a year later
forces.pull: new buyers and their cost next to revenue every week
forces.habit: revenue up means we are growing
forces.anxiety: what if the new and returning split is wrong because of guest checkout

watch.metric: new customers per week and cost per new customer, 7 and 28 day

drives.metric: revenue from new customers per month

jobs.job: When the month is half gone, tell me if we are on track for this month's revenue and gross profit goal and what closes the gap, so I act now and not on the 31st
